title: 100-Day Value Creation Plan
summary: Converting diligence findings into a prioritized first-100-days execution roadmap.
definition: Converting diligence findings into a prioritized first-100-days execution roadmap.
whyItMatters: PE cares because the initiative can convert operating diagnosis into measurable EBITDA, cash flow, growth quality, management accountability, or exit multiple support.
commonProblems: Management has anecdotes but no clean baseline.
The company tracks activity but not value impact.
Owners are unclear and initiatives compete for attention.
diagnosticQuestions: Where is the value leakage visible in the P&L, balance sheet, or operating dashboard?
Which segments, sites, customers, SKUs, vendors, or teams drive the variance?
What can be changed in the first 30, 60, and 100 days without breaking the business?
process: Define the value hypothesis and KPI baseline.
Segment the business to isolate where the opportunity lives.
Prioritize quick wins, structural fixes, and longer-term capability builds.
Assign owners, cadence, and benefits tracking.
Report progress through the value creation dashboard.
ebitdaLogic: The lever improves enterprise value by increasing EBITDA, releasing cash, making growth more durable, or creating a better diligence story that buyers can underwrite.
caseExample: In a sponsor-backed company, the team builds a baseline, targets the highest-variance segments, launches a 100-day sprint, and uses weekly value tracking to separate real savings or growth from one-time noise.
hundredDayPlan: Days 1-30: baseline data, confirm opportunity, name executive owner.
Days 31-60: launch pilots, install dashboard, remove blockers.
Days 61-100: scale what works, lock cadence, quantify run-rate impact.
commonMistakes: Treating the playbook as a one-time project instead of a management system.
Counting theoretical benefits that never hit EBITDA or cash.
Skipping change management with the operating team.

articleSections.title: The 100-Day Sprint: Momentum and Mandate
body: The first 100 days of a private equity investment are the most critical period for establishing the 'mandate for change' and building operational momentum. During this window, the GP must transition from the theoretical assumptions of diligence to the practical realities of daily management, all while maintaining the trust of the legacy management team. A well-executed 100-day plan serves as the 'tactical bridge' between the investment thesis and the long-term Value Creation Plan (VCP), ensuring that no time is wasted in the early months of the hold.

A sophisticated 100-day plan focuses on three primary objectives: establishing visibility, securing the 'low-hanging' financial gains, and upgrading key leadership roles. We utilize this period to install our preferred 'Operating Rhythm,' which includes weekly flash reporting on cash, sales pipeline, and labor productivity. This discipline ensures that the organization understands that 'business as usual' is over and that a new, high-performance culture is being institutionalized across every department.

To manage this rapid transition, we often deploy a dedicated transition team supported by specialized project management tools like Smartsheet or Monday.com. This team is responsible for tracking every workstream against its Day-1, Day-30, and Day-100 milestones, providing the board with a real-time view of implementation progress. By the end of the 100-day sprint, the company should have a stabilized reporting environment and a clear, multi-year roadmap that is fully embraced by the leadership team.
articleSections.callout: The first 100 days define the culture of the hold; if you don't establish pace early, you will never capture it later.

articleSections.title: Establishing Financial Visibility and Controls
body: In many mid-market acquisitions, the existing financial reporting is insufficient for the needs of a private equity GP, making 'Visibility' the top priority for Day 1. We immediately focus on the 'Quote-to-Cash' cycle and the accuracy of the P&L, ensuring that we have a granular understanding of unit economics and margin contribution. This often requires a rapid cleanup of the chart of accounts and the implementation of automated data feeds from legacy ERP systems like QuickBooks or Sage into a modern BI tool like Power BI.

Consider the impact of 'Revenue Leakage' in a service business—without a rigorous 100-day focus on contract compliance, many companies fail to bill for 3-5% of their delivered services. For a $100M revenue business, identifying and closing this gap adds $4M directly to EBITDA without adding a single dollar of incremental cost. At a 12x multiple, this single 100-day initiative creates $48M in enterprise value, effectively paying for the entire transaction's closing costs and then some.

We also install tight 'Cash Controls' within the first week, including a centralized treasury function and a standardized 13-week cash flow forecast. By utilizing tools like Kyriba or HighRadius, we gain real-time visibility into global bank balances and can optimize the 'Cash Conversion Cycle' from the outset. This financial discipline provides the liquidity needed to fund the more capital-intensive operational improvements that will follow in the second and third years of the hold period.

articleSections.title: Leadership Upgrades and Organizational Design
body: The 100-day plan must address the 'People' component of the investment thesis, which often involves upgrading the CFO or adding a specialized COO role. We utilize this period to conduct a formal assessment of the 'Spans and Layers' within the organization to identify structural inefficiencies and 'headcount bloat.' By redesigning the org chart to align with the new VCP, we ensure that every leader has the necessary 'Decision Rights' and accountability to drive their specific value creation levers.

Using organizational design tools like Nakisa or OrgChart, we can visualize the impact of restructuring on the total labor cost and manager-to-employee ratios. Our target is typically to reach an 'Optimal Span of Control' of 7-9 direct reports per manager, which can often lead to a 10-15% reduction in non-sales SG&A. This organizational 'slimming' not only improves EBITDA but also accelerates decision-making by removing redundant layers of management that frequently slow down execution in founder-led businesses.

Furthermore, we use the first 100 days to roll out the Management Equity Plan (MEP) and align the leadership team's incentives with our exit timing. By making the team 'owners' early in the process, we shift their mindset from employees to stakeholders who are personally invested in the success of the 100-day plan. This psychological shift is essential for sustaining the high pace of change required during the transition and for ensuring that the best talent remains committed to the business throughout the hold period.

articleSections.title: Quick Wins: The EBITDA 'Jumpstart'
body: To build credibility with the organization and the investment committee, the 100-day plan must deliver 'Quick Wins' that show immediate P&L impact. These are typically 'non-disruptive' initiatives such as indirect procurement savings, pricing 'tidy-ups,' and the elimination of obviously redundant discretionary spend. We target a minimum of 50-100 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion within the first two quarters simply through better discipline and 'low-complexity' process improvements.

In procurement, we might consolidate the tail-spend and renegotiate contracts for office supplies, shipping, and telecom using a platform like Coupa. Mathematically, for a company with $20M in indirect spend, a 10% reduction through better vendor management adds $2M to EBITDA. This $2M, when magnified by the exit multiple, represents a massive return on the relatively small amount of time and effort required to execute the procurement workstream during the first 100 days.

Pricing is another fertile ground for 100-day wins, where we identify and eliminate 'outlier' discounts and unearned rebates. By utilizing CRM data from Salesforce or HubSpot, we can identify customers who are paying significantly below the median for the same service level. Implementing a 'price floor' or removing 'freight-free' thresholds can drive immediate top-line growth with nearly 100% margin flow-through, providing an early boost to the company's valuation right out of the gate.

articleSections.title: IT and Cybersecurity: Securing the Asset
body: In today's digital environment, no 100-day plan is complete without a rigorous focus on IT infrastructure and cybersecurity. We immediately perform a 'vulnerability scan' and implement baseline security protocols like Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and automated backups to protect the asset from cyber threats. This is not just a risk mitigation exercise; it is also a foundational step in ensuring the company's systems are scalable enough to support the future growth planned in the VCP.

We also assess the 'Technical Debt' inherited from the previous owner, identifying legacy systems that need to be decommissioned or consolidated. If the company is running on three different ERPs due to previous un-integrated acquisitions, we initiate the 'System Convergence' roadmap within the first 60 days. Using tools like Snyk for codebase audits and CrowdStrike for endpoint protection, we ensure that the business is operating on a secure and stable digital foundation from the start.

Finally, we establish a 'Digital Dashboard' that provides the board with real-time uptime and security metrics, ensuring that IT is treated as a core business function rather than a cost center. This focus on IT readiness is critical for the exit, as a modern, secure, and integrated tech stack can command a significant multiple premium. By the end of day 100, the portfolio company should be 'secure by design' and ready for the more complex digital transformations that will drive the next phase of value creation.
